title: Determination of the Resort Credit Issued on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Given Up
content:
When a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass has been given up, resort credit is issued against the pass record for what comes back to the household, and this rule fixes that amount.

**The share of the season still to come.** The share of the season still to come is the days from the handling date to the season's last day set against the days of the season itself.

**The gross amount.** The gross amount coming back is the price committed to on the pass record multiplied by the share of the season still to come, less the tier's day use deduction taken once, and never below zero.

**The scan share.** The gross amount is taken as it stands whatever the pass account shows, a share of 100 per cent.

**The charge retained.** None of the charge retained on the pass being given up is taken off.

**What the protection plan has paid out.** Nothing the protection plan has paid out is taken off.

**The credit uplift.** No uplift is added for taking the value back as resort credit; the figure is taken at a multiple of 1.

**The amount coming back.** The amount coming back is the gross amount taken at the scan share, less the charge retained taken at the offset share and less what the protection plan has paid out taken at the payout share, and the figure that gives is then taken at the credit uplift; it is rounded to the cent once at the end and is never below zero.

### The determination worked through

Hypothetical inputs: a Granite Ridge Collective Unlimited Pass committed to 1490.00, whose day use deduction is 169.00, on a season of 149 days with 60 days still to come on the handling date.

The share of the season still to come is 60 set against 149. The price committed to multiplied by that share is 600.00, and the tier's day use deduction of 169.00 taken once leaves a gross amount of 431.00; neither figure is rounded at those steps. The scan share takes that gross amount as it stands. Nothing is taken off for the charge retained and nothing for what a protection plan has paid out. The figure is then taken at the credit uplift, which leaves it unchanged. Rounded to the cent once at the end, and only there, the resort credit issued is 431.00.
